analysis: The only change in this PR is to docs/developer/test.md. At head lines 2115-2131 it adds documentation for the Model Requant Upload workflow's unit tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models -p 'test_*.py'`). The supplied units are base-text excerpts covering lines 1-926. The changed region (base 2115, head 2115-2131) is outside those excerpts, and only the patch excerpt shows it. The patch is documentation only: no code, no permission, no key or attestation handling, and no wire or storage behavior changes. The added text describes offline tests with a fake aws and python3, a secret-free preflight, a job in the prod environment, master-only runs, a pinned-by-hash toolchain, and an upload gated on a passing check. These are descriptions of test coverage, not security controls, so I could not verify them from the supplied evidence. The related workflow and scripts (scripts/models, the requant workflow) were not supplied, so whether they actually enforce those properties is unverified. The threat model's retained assets and threats (A-004 model weights, T-012, T-027, T-041 cache) are not changed by the doc edit. The doc claims the tests do not establish model quality or serving capacity, which avoids overclaiming. No regression or invalidated assumption found. Residual question: the requant workflow's R2 key-set handling and the prod-environment secret scoping are in other files that this batch did not include.
